findings.detail: The live end() is unscoped and holdInternal() can mark an already active internal operation active again. A late completion from retired same-owner work can therefore release a successor lease.

Live SpbAI.run has no lease acquisition/release wrapper. The isolated candidate wraps run(), captures generation synchronously after successful holdInternal(), and releases that captured generation on both resolve and reject. The real API converts fetch abort/offline outcomes into resolved error objects; those paths were exercised with controlled fetch responses.

Outer finish and MCP cleanup still call legacy end() without a generation. Preserve no-argument compatibility for now, but integrate those callers with captured tokens before relying on generation safety end-to-end. Do not infer full-system safety from this isolated candidate.

candidate_semantics.begin: Retains boolean success/failure and permits only one active lease; every successful acquisition gets a monotonically increasing token.
candidate_semantics.holdInternal: Retains boolean result, rejects when any lease is already active, and creates a new token on success.
candidate_semantics.generation: Returns the active token, or 0 when inactive.
candidate_semantics.end_expected_generation: Returns false and changes no state when the token is stale or there is no active token; returns true and releases the exact active token on match.
candidate_semantics.end_without_argument: Retains legacy release behavior for unconverted callers; this remains unsafe for stale callers and is explicitly listed as an integration gap.
candidate_semantics.core_wrapper: Attempts holdInternal before invoking the asynchronous tool loop, captures generation before provider-await, and ends only that generation on completion/rejection. If acquisition fails, the existing core behavior continues without claiming a lease so nested externally/outer-owned calls remain compatible.

validation.result: PASS, 12 assertion groups; controlled fetch only; zero provider calls, zero native calls.
validation.scope_limit: Isolated candidate behavior only. Parent must integrate candidate and tokenized outer callers, then run native/MCP lifecycle acceptance.
